SAN FRANCISCO-This maritime metropolis 1623
has a spectacular setting. Its landlocked harbor is one
of the world's finest. Connecting it with the mainland
are the 4½-mile San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge,
the world's longest, and the Golden Gate, whose
4,200-foot main span makes it the longest suspen-
sion bridge. On Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay
is the notorious Federal penitentiary. The Municipal,
Airport is the take-off point for connecting flights to
the Pacific and the Far East.
OAKLAND - Fast-growing industrial city,
terminus of three transcontinental railroads
home of over 100 nationally known manufacturers.
SAN JOSE-Large cannery and dried fruit 1583
packing center. Shipping point for prunes and ap-
ricots. At Lick Observatory, northeast of town on the
western slope of Mount Hamilton, more than 30
comets and 4,800 double stars have been found and
charted, as well as six satellites of Jupiter.
YOSEMITE NAT. PARK-Spectacular moun
tain scenery embracing the Sierra Nevada range. It
is noted for its lofty waterfalls, precipitous cliffs and
gorges, and three great sequoia groves.
MADERA-Sweet wine in great quantities is
produced from surrounding vineyards.
FRIANT DAM-A concrete dam, 3,430 feet
long, 320 feet high, on the San Joaquin 20 miles
from Fresno. It backs up a reservoir 15 miles long.
FRESNO-Hub of fertile San Joaquin Val-
ley, completely surrounded by vast vineyard acreage.

HOOVER DAM-Highest in the world, in 1174
Black Canyon of the Colorado River. This concrete
dam is 726 feet high and 1,244 feet along the crest.
Flood-lighted at night, it is an impressive sight along
the Flagship route. Lake Mead, its reservoir, has a
550-mile shoreline.
GRAND CANYON NAT. PARK - The mile- 1030
deep gorge of the
Colorado River, 4 to 18 miles
wide, affords a breath-taking panorama of fantastic
color. More than half of the 217-mile river gorge,
world's greatest example of stream erosion, is within
the park. During daylight hours, Flagship passengers
can see all the major wonders of the area.
NAVAJO INDIAN RESERVATION-Evidences 1012

PAINTED DESERT-Mineral-laden sands,
multi-colored gullies and bluffs extend for 300 miles
along the north bank of the Little Colorado River.
